Bitcoin Electrical Cost — Falsification Backtest

Claim tested: “Bitcoin NEVER drops below its electrical cost of production.” Price = consensus daily OHLC (Bitstamp / Coinbase / Kraken). Cost models A (CBECI), B (bottom-up), C (Capriole if provided).

Does the claim hold? NO

NO — the literal claim is false. Using consensus low_median vs Model A electrical cost, price traded below the line on 14 days (first 2018-11-24). Model B bottom-up: 0 days. Capriole-style production cost (electrical/0.6) was breached on 1664 days. CBECI's 2023 downward history revision reduces how often Model A looks breached ex-post — see caveats.

Sensitivity

Question answered: at what assumption does the “floor” stop being a floor? When breach_days > 0 the literal claim fails for that parameter set. Higher $/kWh or worse efficiency (multiplier > 1 on Model B) raises the cost line and increases breaches.

Methodological caveats

  • Reflexivity / circularity: Hashrate follows price, so the cost line rises with bull markets and falls after crashes (miner capitulation lowers difficulty). The “floor” partly moves to meet price and is not an independent support level.
  • Unknown inputs: Global $/kWh and fleet efficiency are assumptions. Small changes move the line by thousands of dollars (JPMorgan estimated ~$4,300 per 1¢/kWh in 2023). See the sensitivity heatmaps. At $0.03/kWh Model A never breaches; at $0.08/kWh it is below cost on ~25% of days — the “floor” is an assumption, not a law.
  • Look-ahead bias: CBECI revised methodology in 2023 and revised history downward. Under today’s revised series, Nov 2022 (FTX) does not breach Model A electrical cost (~$14K) even though price sat near $16K; it does breach Capriole-style production cost (electrical/0.6). Capriole charts can also lag by weeks. The line you see today may not be what was visible in real time.
  • Venue differences: Single-exchange wicks (e.g. COVID crash prints) can create or erase breaches. Every test is run on both low_min and low_median.
  • Survivorship and small n: Independent Model A electrical breach episodes number only about four in this sample. Forward-return stats are illustrative, not a trading system backtest with meaningful statistical power.
